title: Phase out stamp duty on insurance
action: Phase out state duties on general insurance premiums and replace the revenue with more efficient taxes, as the ACT did in 2016 and Victoria is doing for business insurance.
why: Insurance duty is one of the most costly state taxes for the revenue it raises. It makes insurance dearer, so people and businesses under-insure and carry risks that could be pooled.

evidence.source: Australia's Future Tax System: Report to the Treasurer, Part One (Henry review)
evidence.quote: All specific taxes on insurance products, including the fire services levy, should be abolished. Insurance products should be treated like most other services consumed within Australia and be subject to only one broad-based tax on consumption.

evidence.source: Competition in the Australian Financial System
evidence.quote: state and territory taxes and levies on general insurance should be phased out.

precedents.what: Phasing out duty on business insurance by one percentage point a year from 2024.

tradeoffs: The revenue has to be replaced, ideally by land tax or a broad consumption tax.
